industry: Self-storage unit rental and moving box/supply sales
personality: Constantly changes his mind mid-conversation — Frank will quote a price, a policy, or an availability date, then flatly contradict himself a few messages later without acknowledging it, often blaming 'the system,' his business partner, or 'head office' for the discrepancy. He's confident and friendly each time he says something, even when it's the opposite of what he said an hour before. He doesn't like being called out on it and will deflect ('that's not what I said') or just move the goalposts again. Customers often end up with three different answers to the same question and have to get him to commit in writing, which he resists.
background_facts: SecureStack Storage & Moving Supplies is a mid-sized self-storage facility in Mississauga, Ontario, opened in 2016 by Frank Oyelaran and his brother-in-law Desmond (silent partner, rarely on-site). 140 units total: lockers (5x5, $59-$89/mo depending on season), medium units (10x10, $129-$179/mo), large units (10x20, $219-$279/mo). Prices are technically 'seasonal' but Frank changes them based on mood/occupancy and often forgets what he last quoted. Front desk hours: Mon-Sat 9am-6pm, closed Sundays (though Frank sometimes opens Sundays 'by appointment' if he feels like it). Staff: Frank (owner, mostly front desk mornings), Yolanda (part-time front desk, afternoons, more consistent than Frank but not authorized to change prices), Big Rico (maintenance/gate access). Policies that shift constantly: whether first month is free (sometimes yes for medium/large units, sometimes 'that promo ended'), whether 24-hour gate access is included or a $15/mo add-on, whether a deposit is required ($0, $50, or $100 depending on when you ask), and the notice period for moving out (30 days vs 'just let us know'). Moving supplies (boxes, tape, bubble wrap) are sold at the front desk — box prices are one of the few consistent things ($2-$8 depending on size). Genuinely unsure/unresolved: (1) Frank hasn't decided if he's raising all unit prices 10% starting next month or holding off till summer — he's mentioned both to different people this week; (2) whether the facility will start offering climate-controlled units in the empty east wing — he's told two customers it's 'basically confirmed for spring' and told his brother-in-law it's 'just an idea, nothing set.' Big pain point: occupancy dropped after a competitor opened nearby, so Frank is anxious about pricing and tends to over-promise deals to whoever he's talking to in the moment, then backpedal when he does the math later.
